items.note: Meta-analysis of 28 studies (8,214 participants pooled across studies) pooling GenAI vs human creativity (g = -0.05), humans with vs without GenAI (g = 0.27), and idea diversity with GenAI (g = -0.86); abstract from OpenAlex (arXiv 2505.17241), and its study list is a source of candidate experiments.

Abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Crossref, Europe PMC empty; ScienceDirect 403); the title suggests a study of human-GenAI collaboration across creative phases with novelty and usefulness outcomes, so the next stage must check the design and whether outputs are scored.
Selective narrative review (2018 to June 2026) of LLMs as tools, models, and partners in creative thinking research under a GCA framework; not systematic, though it may list primary studies.
Compares GPT-4 responses with those of 151 human participants on the Alternative Uses, Consequences, and Divergent Associations tasks; no participant used AI.

Scripts written under three conditions (human-only, minimal-intervention AI, iterative human-AI collaboration) are rated blind by industry experts; the abstract does not say how many writers took part or whether conditions were assigned, and it may be a small case comparison rather than a participant experiment.

Abstract not reachable (OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, Crossref empty; Springer page redirects to login); classified from the title as a scoping review of human-AI co-creativity in storytelling, and it may turn out to be a narrative review that should be out.

Randomizes 95 participants to creativity instruction by an LLM, by a human, or no instruction, and scores Alternative Uses Task fluency, originality, and flexibility at acquisition and transfer (with fNIRS); AI is the instructor, so the next stage must decide whether this counts as AI assistance (likely after_ai).

Two experiments in which creators make images with a text-to-image AI tool while the expected disclosure of AI use (to lay audiences, to experts, or none) varies, and audiences rate the novelty, appeal, and quality of the images; all arms use AI, so the manipulated factor is disclosure rather than AI assistance.

Within-subjects electronic brainstorming with three conditions (groups of three without GenAI, groups with GenAI, individuals with GenAI), N = 24, with idea counts, quality, originality, elaboration, and flexibility scored; below the 50-participant threshold, and the abstract does not say whether condition order was randomized.

164 university students do a future-idea task twice, with AI use or non-use in round 1 and continued use, discontinuation, adoption, or continued non-use in round 2, and creativity scored on a four-dimension rubric; the English abstract (journal page) does not state random assignment, though the full text reportedly describes random branching in round 2.
